title: Infrastructure Errors
description: Design error responses for infrastructure failures including database outages, downstream service failures, and gateway timeouts.

data.text: Infrastructure errors happen when your API cannot fulfill a request due to downstream failures, not client mistakes. These errors should be transient-safe, include retry guidance, and never leak internal architecture details.

data.title: 504 Gateway Timeout with retry guidance
data.content: The API proxies a request to a downstream payment service that times out.
data.code:
GET /payments/ord_991

Response: 504 Gateway Timeout
{
  "type": "https://api.example.com/errors/gateway-timeout",
  "title": "Gateway Timeout",
  "status": 504,
  "requestId": "req_gw_001",
  "message": "The payment service did not respond in time.",
  "retry": {
    "shouldRetry": true,
    "retryAfterMs": 2000,
    "maxRetries": 3
  },
  "documentationUrl": "https://docs.example.com/errors/gateway-timeout"
}

items: Set strict timeouts on all downstream calls: 3s for DB, 5s for APIs, 10s for file operations
Return 504 immediately when a downstream call times out; do not wait for a response that will never come
Include Retry-After: 2 (seconds) on 503 responses to give the infrastructure time to recover
Do not retry non-idempotent requests (POST without idempotency key) on timeout

data.title: 503 when circuit breaker is open
data.content: After 5 consecutive downstream failures, the circuit breaker opens and returns 503 immediately.
data.code:
POST /orders

Response: 503 Service Unavailable
{
  "type": "https://api.example.com/errors/service-unavailable",
  "title": "Service Unavailable",
  "status": 503,
  "requestId": "req_cb_001",
  "message": "The payment service is temporarily unavailable.",
  "retry": {
    "shouldRetry": true,
    "retryAfterMs": 5000,
    "maxRetries": 3,
    "circuitState": "open"
  },
  "documentationUrl": "https://status.example.com"
}

data.title: Infrastructure errors are not your fault
data.text: A 503 from your API is not a bug in your code. It is a signal that the system is temporarily overloaded. Clients that receive 503 should retry with backoff, not give up and show a generic error page.

items.question: Should I return 500 or 502 for downstream failures?
items.answer: Use 502 Bad Gateway when the downstream returned a non-success response. Use 504 Gateway Timeout when the downstream did not respond in time. Use 503 Service Unavailable when your own server is overloaded.

items.question: How do I prevent retry storms?
items.answer: Use exponential backoff with jitter: retry after 1s, 2s, 4s with +/- 30% random jitter. Do not retry immediately after failure. For 503, honor the Retry-After header.

items.question: Should I expose the downstream error message?
items.answer: Never. Map downstream errors to your own error codes and messages. A downstream 500 might mean anything; your client only needs to know that the operation failed and can be retried.

data.title: Key takeaway
points: Infrastructure errors must be transient-safe and include retry guidance.
Use 502 for downstream errors, 504 for timeouts, 503 for overload.
Never expose internal service names or stack traces.
Circuit breakers prevent retry storms from overwhelming downstream.
data.takeaway: Infrastructure errors are opportunities to build resilience. Design them so clients automatically back off and recover without human intervention.
